detail: The case's key expectation is that the browser navigates to /user/orders. The test asserts toHaveURL and calls demo.caption('Redirected to ...'), but no keyframe (05-08) shows that caption, and the recording has no address bar, so the video never shows the redirect URL. Narrate the URL so it is visible in the highlight frames.

After step 4 the case expects navigation to /user/orders. The test captions 'Redirected to ...', but keyframes 10 and 11 show the orders list with no caption or URL, so the redirect after fixing Address is not visible in the video.

The case's main expected result is that the browser navigates to /user/orders. The spec calls demo.caption(`Redirected to ${page.url()}`) before the highlights, but keyframes 05-09 show only the checkout page and then My orders with no caption, so the video never shows the URL after the redirect (lesson L2). Wait until My orders has finished loading before setting the caption, then re-record.

After step 4 the case expects the browser to navigate to /user/orders. The 'Redirected to' caption the spec sets does not appear in keyframes 10-13, which show My orders with one $249.99 order but no URL. The 'Still on …/checkout' and 'Separate tab …/user/orders' captions do show.

The highlights after the 1st and 2nd checkout show the My orders list (one, then two $249.99 orders), but no caption shows the URL the browser landed on (/user/orders), unlike TC-03 and TC-06, which use captionRedirect. The recording has no address bar, so the video cannot show that each single click landed on My orders.

The test asserts toHaveURL(/user/orders) after each checkout, but neither My orders highlight (frames 05 and 10) has a caption showing the redirected URL, and no caption marks the second checkout as a newly loaded /checkout. The other cases narrate this with captionRedirect or 'Opened <url>'.
